extracted.intended_audience: authors, handling editors, specialty chief editors, and peer reviewers participating in Frontiers journal peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and quality standards for submission, review, editorial decision-making, and conduct in Frontiers journals, including acceptance/rejection criteria, reviewer/editor duties, the independent and interactive review phases, and arbitration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: VALID acceptance criteria (V A L I D)
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions accepted at Frontiers must be VALID: V: valid research question and hypothesis with a relevant theory; A: applies correct and transparent methodology, with study design and materials clearly laid out; L: language and presentation are clear and adequate, and figures/tables meet scientific norms; I: in line with Frontiers author guidelines on editorial and ethical policies; D: determined by grounding in existing literature through sufficient referencing and appropriate coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts accepted only if they meet all parts of VALID. See author guidelines and Frontiers policies for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective methodological errors (rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission may be rejected if there are clear objective errors in the methodology of the study design, data collection, or analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective errors preventing valid conclusions can justify immediate rejection at any stage (initial validation, peer review, final validation, or post-acceptance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / plagiarism / duplication (rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript must conform to editorial policies by being original; it will be rejected if plagiarized or a duplication of previous work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research integrity team screens for originality; plagiarism or duplicate publication are grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and presentation quality (rejection / reviewability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The language and presentation must be of sufficient quality for a rigorous and efficient peer review to take place; otherwise the manuscript can be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and tables should meet scientific norms; poor presentation that prevents proper review is a rejection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical compliance (rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts violating ethical policies — e.g., not complying with privacy protection guidelines, lacking ethical review board approval, or failing internationally recognized standards for research with humans or animals — may be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ethical concerns are identified at any stage, chief editors and the Chief Executive Editor will investigate and may reject the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and research integrity violations (rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will be rejected if authors have not adhered to authorship guidelines or have fabricated or falsified data, or manipulated images/figures deceitfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research integrity team performs pre- and post-review quality screens; fabrication/falsification/image manipulation lead to rejection and possible institutional referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biased references (rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: References that are clearly biased (geographical bias, excessive self-citation, school-of-thought bias, or citation cartels) and do not reflect the current status of knowledge can be grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and editors assess whether referencing appropriately covers relevant literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misleading conclusions / public health risk (rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies whose conclusions are misleading due to biased or faulty analyses — and that could pose a public health threat — may be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers must evaluate whether conclusions are supported by data and analyses; risk to public health increases grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudoscientific research questions (rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions investigating pseudoscientific research questions are listed as a reason for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope and scientific validity are evaluated at pre-screening and during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer and editor subject-matter expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers must be experts in the manuscript's subject, with necessary expertise demonstrated by an established research or publication record in the same or related area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial review operations team ensures appropriate expertise; lack of expertise can lead to revocation and replacement of reviewers/editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers must have no relationship to the authors and/or research that would affect the objectivity of the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conflicts of interest are discovered during review, the individuals can be revoked and replaced; failure to disclose collaborations/manipulation leads to termination of involvement and may trigger institutional notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: No coercive citation requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors or reviewers must not inappropriately request the citation of their own papers or the journal's articles (coercive citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inappropriate coercive citation requests can result in revocation/replacement and monitoring; valid academic reasons must be conveyed for any requested citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough completion of subject-specific review questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate manuscripts using a quality assessment tool and designated review questionnaire adapted to each article type, prioritizing scientific quality, rigor, and validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must thoroughly complete these templates to assess methodology solidity, rigor, and whether conclusions are supported by sufficient data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive, verifiable review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Review reports must provide a constructive assessment of the manuscript's validity and quality; review reports are verified to ensure they provide such constructive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports are reviewed by the editorial operations team and may be checked for adequacy; reports that are non-constructive or suspicious may result in sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final editorial checks of peer-review adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Final editorial checks verify that the peer-review process adhered to quality standards, that reviewers' and editors' concerns have been addressed, and that the manuscript is ready for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final checks fail, the manuscript may be returned to review or provisional acceptance overridden and rejected without publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct, timeliness, and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers must submit thorough, high-quality review reports, provide feedback in a timely manner, remain responsive and collaborate with authors, and behave professionally and constructively in communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants who fail to meet conduct or timeliness expectations may be removed from assignments; authors unresponsive for extended periods (30 days) risk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection and sanctioning of peer-review manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Manipulative behaviors (fake identities, fake/deceptive review reports, peer review rings, or manipulated peer review process) will result in termination of involvement in peer review and rejection of ongoing submissions, with issues raised with institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frontiers actively monitors for such behaviors; discovery at any stage triggers investigation and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum reviewer number and majority endorsement for acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Most article types require at least two reviewers; acceptance requires an editor and the minimum number of independent reviewers assigned for the article type and endorsement by a majority of the assigned, non-withdrawn reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the minimum number of endorsing reviewers is not met, the handling editor must recommend rejection to the specialty chief editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review phase timeline and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: During the independent review phase, reviewers assess the manuscript independently and submit the standardized independent review report within ten days after accepting the assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each reviewer submits independently; handling editor is notified when reports are submitted and can activate interactive review after all reports are in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive review phase and author response deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interactive review phase, authors and reviewers interact via a collaborative forum; authors are asked to respond and/or submit a revised manuscript within seven, ten, or 14 days depending on revision level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors are unresponsive to multiple attempts, a final email with a seven-day deadline is sent; failure to respond can lead to manuscript withdrawal from review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling editor responsibilities and decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The handling editor is accountable for inviting and overseeing expert reviewers, validating reviewer recommendations in line with acceptance/rejection criteria, seeking further expert feedback if they disagree with reviewers, and making acceptance decisions (which may be later overruled by chief editors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling editors most often follow reviewers' recommendations; they may request additional reviewers or escalate to specialty chief editor as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short peer review variant for certain article types
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorials, Classifications, and Grand Challenges undergo a shortened peer review: they are forwarded directly to the interactive review phase and may be reviewed by the handling editor alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive review, acceptance, and rejection follow the same rules as full peer reviews despite the shortened initial procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration for disputed rejections (author-triggered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may rebut a rejection and trigger arbitration by providing factual, constructive information (e.g., ethics committee letters) so an informed decision can be made; editorial office arbitrates and may call independent experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbitration timelines vary from weeks to months with updates every 2–4 weeks; arbitration can reinstate a manuscript to the stage where rejection occurred or restart peer review with new editors/reviewers if ruled in favor of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-triggered arbitration
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can trigger arbitration if they judge authors reluctant to make required changes; reviewers may recommend rejection or withdraw, and if arbitration rules in favor of authors, the manuscript can be accepted despite prior rejection recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer withdrawal requires recruiting a replacement and may slow the process; identity of reviewers remains undisclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance prerequisites and final validation
rubrics_metrics.description: For acceptance to be considered the manuscript must be VALID, have an editor and minimum independent reviewers assigned, and be endorsed by a majority of assigned, non-withdrawn reviewers; after handling editor acceptance the article enters final validation checks by Frontiers' peer review team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final validation includes technical and quality checks of the review; failure at this stage can return the manuscript to review or result in rejection prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance checks and possible post-acceptance rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts can be rejected post-acceptance if issues are identified late-stage during Frontiers' final checks or research integrity screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is provisional until final validation and APC payment; rejection after provisional acceptance carries no APC charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article processing charge (APC) payment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The APC is payable within 30 days of acceptance and is required before final publication of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a manuscript is rejected, no APC or other fee is charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant removal and sanctions for non-adherence to review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants in peer review will be removed from assignments if they do not meet review standards (expertise, conduct, timeliness); editors and reviewers may be revoked and removed from editorial board membership for misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions include removal from assignments, revocation of editorial roles, termination of involvement, and reporting to institutions for malfeasance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer withdrawal and retention of submitted reports
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewer can withdraw from the review at any time or recommend rejection; if they withdraw after submitting an independent review report, that report is maintained in the review forum and not removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawn reviewers no longer participate in the forum but can continue to follow manuscript status via My Frontiers.
